direct: NGINX Open Source and Plus from 1.9.5 with HTTP/2 can be made to run code as the nginx worker without a login; fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and proof-of-concept code is public for one flaw.
downstream: Xint chained one flaw with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root and escape a Docker container, so a web front end can become a host compromise.

NGINX is embedded in load balancers, Kubernetes ingress controllers and appliances that update on their vendors' schedules; Synology has already listed the same CVE in DSM, so expect more appliance advisories.
watch_for: Ingress and appliance vendors shipping fixed NGINX builds
Worker crashes on HTTP/2 traffic
A Linux kernel fix and CVE for the SCTP flaw
Reports of in-the-wild exploitation
Appliance advisories naming CVE-2026-123007

direct: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication on VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8); Google says ARMORY CASTLE exploited it as a zero-day, and Rapid7 reports activity from as early as September. Fixes include vCenter 8.0 U3m; there is no workaround.
downstream: vCenter controls every virtual machine it manages, so one compromised server can expose a whole virtual estate.
Exploitation predates the fix, so patching does not show whether a server was already entered; logs back to September matter.
watch_for: vCenter servers reachable from untrusted networks
Unexpected vCenter sign-ins or new local accounts
Hunting guidance and indicators from Google and Broadcom
Victims named in follow-up reporting

direct: GreyNoise says GT13 used 99 IP addresses against Check Point Security Management Servers from Oct 17 to Nov 2, reaching at least 22 organisations, running over 100 management tasks and taking data from 24 servers; it lists CVE-2026-16232 among the flaws.
downstream: A management server holds policy, credentials and configuration for every gateway it manages, so a compromise there can change or expose firewall rules across the estate (our inference from how the product works).
Victims that have not checked management-server logs since October may not know they were reached.
watch_for: A Check Point advisory or CISA KEV entry for CVE-2026-16232
Unexpected management tasks or admin sessions in SmartConsole audit logs since Oct 17
Policy pushes nobody scheduled
Further GT13 reporting or attribution

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after a vulnerability was exploited on Nov 13; its own account emails and contacts were taken, and customer data of several hundred companies was affected in each data category. It plans a phased restart in mid-January 2027.
downstream: Customers report the scale: DHC about 19.11 million records, ZOZO about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers, SMBC up to about 14 million, Marui about 8.83 million, MUFG Bank about 6.5 million, plus Sharp, Mitsumo, Timee, Mainichi Shimbun, Schoo and PLUS.

Leaked profiles (names, emails, dates of birth, purchase attributes, and for some Marui card members income) make convincing phishing in Japanese; integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems.
Companies that ended their KARTE contract are included, so former customers should check too.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names, member IDs and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE
Regulator action by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission

direct: KEPCO says personal data of over 1.5 million people (a simple sum, overlap unchecked) leaked from its Hanjeon ON customer platform and SRM procurement system, including resident registration, bank account and card numbers; it believes an outside attacker broke in, blocked external IP access, suspended some services and asked police to investigate.
downstream: Inferred: resident registration numbers with bank and card details are the material for fraud and for convincing phishing that poses as KEPCO bills or refunds.
Inferred: the SRM system serves KEPCO suppliers, so supplier staff may receive targeted phishing posing as KEPCO procurement.
watch_for: KEPCO notices naming exactly what each person lost
Electricity bill or refund phishing in Korean
PIPC or police findings on how the attacker got in
Suppliers reporting phishing that uses procurement details

direct: The Commission confirmed a campaign it calls AI-generated, detected Oct 22, that took applications offline, and on Nov 23 that names and email addresses were stolen from its EU Academy learning platform.
downstream: EU Academy users were notified and should expect phishing that uses the Commission's name; the Commission itself warned of this.
Euronews, citing two sources, reports a suspected China-backed actor and an attack not fully contained, which would keep EU institutions and their contacts in scope.
watch_for: Phishing posing as EU Academy or Commission HR
A formal attribution or CERT-EU guidance
Confirmation the intrusion is contained
Notices from other EU bodies sharing the affected systems
who_should_care: Public bodies working with the Commission

direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected x86-64 HotSpot Java runtime could be crashed or taken over without a login; CISA said to patch immediately.
downstream: Siemens says every version of its Industrial Edge Management products is affected and has no fix yet, only the advice to block internet access, so the flaw reaches factory software.
Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build and depends on each vendor shipping a new runtime.
watch_for: Unexpected JVM crashes and restarts
Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Siemens fix releases for Industrial Edge
Signs of exploitation reported by CISA or vendors

direct: Amazon says AI agents run through the open-source Cairn tool found and exploited a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label within 11 minutes of mapping its API and gained root; a fix came on Nov 18.
downstream: The operator then gave the agents a proxy into a second university network running the same software, so one exposed research server can lead to others.
Medical imaging research platforms hold patient-derived data and often run outside central IT's patch cycle.
If agents can find a zero-day this quickly, the time between exposure and compromise for niche, internet-facing tools shrinks to minutes.
watch_for: MONAI Label servers reachable from the internet
Unexpected file uploads or new root processes on research servers
Amazon indicators and further victims
Other Cairn-driven campaigns

direct: GL.iNet says an unauthorized party exploited a flaw in its cloud remote management service to install malicious software on some GL.iNet routers and KVM devices; it fixed the cloud flaw and blocked the access used, and is still determining scope.
downstream: GL.iNet says the fix does not remove malware from devices already infected, so owners must check and clean devices themselves.
A KVM device gives keyboard, screen and power control of the machine it is attached to, so an infected KVM can reach servers behind it (our inference from what the device does).
watch_for: GL.iNet guidance on how to detect and remove the malware
Unexpected outbound traffic from GL.iNet routers and KVMs
Devices enrolled in GL.iNet cloud management that nobody uses
who_should_care: Data centre and lab admins using IP KVMs

direct: Wiz reports that successful attacks by agent frameworks such as ARTEX grew sharply over three weeks, with about twenty further incidents disclosed by vendors, from several unrelated operators; CSIRT Italia and New Zealand's NCSC issued warnings in the same days.
downstream: Agents scan, exploit and move through many organisations at once, so time from public exploit to compromise shrinks (our inference from the cases on file).
Because the tools are open source and copied, takedowns of one build do not stop use, as NZ's NCSC described.
watch_for: Bursts of exploitation across many targets within hours
ARTEX indicators published by Wiz or CERTs
Victim notices that describe "agentic" or "AI-generated" intrusions
Exploited CVEs listed by CSIRT Italia
